title: Drill 3 · Word Problem Workout 📝
subject: Maths
source_note: Mistake_Tracker 2026-07-10, 2026-07-17, topictest4 cross-cutting pattern: right method, wrong or unfinished final answer. Plus Maths_Brain Priority #3/#5 and Oxford Yr8 8G

questions.stem: A bakery sells cupcakes and muffins in the ratio 5 : 3. On Monday it sold 120 more cupcakes than muffins.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: How many muffins were sold on Monday?

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: What fraction of all the items sold on Monday were cupcakes? (e.g. 2/7)

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: On Tuesday it sold the same total number of items, but in the ratio 3 : 5. How many MORE muffins were sold on Tuesday than on Monday?

solution: Difference in units: 5 − 3 = 2 units = 120, so 1 unit = 60.
(c) Tuesday muffins = 5/8 of 480 = 300. More than Monday: 300 − 180 = 120.
questions.technique: Ratio + difference: the DIFFERENCE in units equals the given difference. Find 1 unit first.
questions.trap: (c) asks for 'how many MORE', not Tuesday's muffins (300)
questions.source: Mistake_Tracker 2026-07-10 P2 Q16 (3-day ratio problem left unfinished)

asks_for.prompt: Before you start: what does part (c) want?
options: How many MORE muffins on Tuesday than Monday

questions.stem: A water tank was 3/4 full. After Mia used 21 L, the tank was 2/5 full.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: What is the capacity of the tank?

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: How many more litres are needed now to fill the tank to the top?

solution: The 21 L she used = 3/4 − 2/5 of the tank = 15/20 − 8/20 = 7/20.
7/20 = 21 L, so 1/20 = 3 L and the full tank (20/20) = 60 L.
(b) It is 2/5 full, so 3/5 is empty: 3/5 × 60 = 36 L.
questions.technique: Fraction change = amount used. Then re-read: capacity, water left, or space left?
questions.trap: Writing the given 21 L as an answer, or giving the water still in the tank (24 L)
questions.source: Mistake_Tracker 2026-07-10 P2 Q11 (container: right working, wrong final value)

options: The water in the tank now

questions.stem: Tom, Ava and Leo collect stickers. Ava has 4 times as many as Tom. Leo has 15 fewer than Ava. Together they have 165 stickers.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: How many stickers does Tom have?

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: How many stickers does Leo have?

questions.technique: Name each person with the same letter. At the end, underline WHO the question asks about.
questions.source: Mistake_Tracker 2026-07-17 P2 Q6 (answered the wrong named person)

questions.stem: A jacket costs $160. It is reduced by 25%. Then a further 10% is taken off the SALE price.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: What single percentage discount would give the same final price?

solution: (b) Total saved = $160 − $108 = $52. $52 ÷ $160 × 100 = 32.5%. (Not 35%: the 10% came off a smaller amount.)
questions.technique: Percentage chains: each % comes off the NEW amount. Discounts don't simply add.

questions.stem: In a 25-question quiz, a correct answer scores 4 points and a wrong answer loses 1 point. A blank scores 0. Zoe answered every question and scored 70.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: How many questions did Zoe get right?

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: If she had left her wrong ones blank instead, what would her score have been?

solution: If all 25 were right: 100 points. Each wrong one changes +4 into −1, which costs 5 points.
100 − 70 = 30 points lost, and 30 ÷ 5 = 6 wrong. So 25 − 6 = 19 right.
questions.technique: Assume everything is right, then work out what each swap costs.

questions.stem: A fish tank is 60 cm long, 30 cm wide and 40 cm high. It is filled with water to 3/4 of its height.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: How many litres of water are in the tank?

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Water drains out at 1.5 L per minute. How many minutes until the water is 10 cm deep?

questions.technique: Tank problems: use the WATER height, not the tank height. Then cm³ ÷ 1000 = L.
questions.trap: Using the full 40 cm height (72 L), or draining it all (36 min)

questions.stem: A train leaves at 9:47 am and arrives at 1:12 pm. The trip is 246 km.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: How long is the trip in minutes?

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: What is the train's average speed?

questions.technique: Elapsed time: count up to the next hour, then whole hours, then the leftover minutes.
